title: Candle Care & Safety
text: Candle Care & Safety — Candle Care & Safety: Last updated: 29 September 2026 A little care goes a long way with candles. Follow these simple steps and you'll get a cleaner, more even burn, a stronger scent and the full burn time from every Thistle & Pine candle.

title: Candle Care & Safety
text: Candle Care & Safety — The first burn matters most: The first time you light your candle, let it burn for 2–3 hours , until the melted wax reaches the edges of the container. This is called a full melt pool. Wax has a "memory". If you blow it out too early on the first burn, it will tend to melt only to that point every time afterwards, creating a tunnel down the middle and wasting wax around the sides.

title: Candle Care & Safety
text: Candle Care & Safety — Trim the wick: Before every burn, trim the wick to 5mm . A wick that's too long produces a large, flickering flame, soot and black marks on the glass. Use a wick trimmer or scissors, and remove the trimmings from the wax before lighting.

title: Candle Care & Safety
text: Candle Care & Safety — Don't burn for too long: Never burn a candle for more than 4 hours at a time. After 4 hours, carbon can build up on the wick, making the flame unstable and the container very hot. Blow it out, let it cool completely, trim the wick and relight later.

title: Candle Care & Safety
text: Candle Care & Safety — Burn times: Candle size | Approximate burn time Large | About 45 hours Small | About 25 hours Burn times are approximate and assume the wick is trimmed to 5mm and each burn lasts no longer than 4 hours.

title: Candle Care & Safety
text: Candle Care & Safety — Candle safety: Never leave a burning candle unattended. Keep candles out of reach of children and pets. Place on a stable, heat-resistant surface, away from draughts, curtains, shelves and anything flammable. Keep burning candles at least 10cm apart. Don't move a candle while it's lit or while the wax is liquid. Stop using the candle when around 1cm of wax remains at the bottom, as the container can overheat. Extinguish with a snuffer or by gently blowing it out – never use water.

title: Candle Care & Safety
text: Candle Care & Safety — Storing your candles: Keep candles in a cool, dark place with the lid on. Heat and direct sunlight can fade the colour and weaken the fragrance.

title: Candle Care & Safety
text: Candle Care & Safety — Reusing the container: Once your candle has finished, pour a little boiling water into the container to loosen the remaining wax, let it cool, then pop the wax out. The clean container makes a lovely pot for pens, make-up brushes or small plants.

title: Candle Care & Safety
text: Candle Care & Safety — Something not right?: If your candle tunnels despite following this guide, or the wick won't stay lit, contact us with your order number and a photo. Candles are covered by our standard 12-month warranty. If you believe a candle has caused a fire, burn or other safety hazard, stop using it and call us on 0113 496 0321 straight away. A member of our team will handle your case personally.

text: Damaged or Faulty Items — Damaged or Faulty Items: Last updated: 9 June 2026 We pack every order carefully, but occasionally something arrives damaged or develops a fault. We're sorry if that's happened to you – here's how we'll put it right.

title: Damaged or Faulty Items
text: Damaged or Faulty Items — Items damaged in transit: If your item arrives broken, cracked, dented or otherwise damaged, please let us know within 48 hours of delivery . To help us resolve it quickly, send us: your order number a photo of the damaged item a photo of the packaging, including the outer box and shipping label You can send these by email to support@thistleandpine.co.uk or upload them through live chat on our website. Please keep the item and packaging until we've been in touch, as the courier may need to see them.

title: Damaged or Faulty Items
text: Damaged or Faulty Items — Faulty items: A faulty item is one that isn't of satisfactory quality, isn't fit for purpose or doesn't match its description. Your rights are protected by the Consumer Rights Act 2015: When the fault appears | What you're entitled to Within 30 days of delivery | A full refund From 30 days up to 6 months | A repair or replacement (or a refund if that isn't possible) After 6 months | Covered by our product warranty All our products come with a 12-month warranty from delivery. Furniture and electrical items such as kettles, toasters and lamps have a 2-year warranty, and our Pine Pro cookware carries a 10-year guarantee against manufacturing defects.

title: Damaged or Faulty Items
location: § Returning a damaged or faulty item
text: Damaged or Faulty Items — Returning a damaged or faulty item: We pay the return postage for any damaged or faulty item. Once you've reported the problem, our team will send you a prepaid label or, for large 2-person delivery items, arrange a free collection – the usual £25 collection fee does not apply to faulty goods. For low-value items costing under £20, we may refund you without needing the item back. We'll let you know if this applies to you. If the item was faulty, we'll also refund the original delivery charge.

title: Damaged or Faulty Items
text: Damaged or Faulty Items — What isn't covered: Normal wear and tear, accidental damage and damage caused by not following the care instructions aren't treated as faults. For example: rust or a damaged surface on cast iron that has been put in the dishwasher warping or discolouration from overheating a pan on a high flame when empty splitting of a wooden board that has been soaked in water scratches on non-stick coatings caused by metal utensils Our care guides explain how to look after each product so it lasts.

title: Damaged or Faulty Items

Your card provider may apply its own exchange rate or foreign transaction fee.

If your item is faulty or arrived damaged, we'll cover the cost of returning it. We recommend using a tracked service when sending a return, as we can't refund items that don't reach us.

text: Changing or Cancelling an Order — Changing or Cancelling an Order: Last updated: 22 July 2026 Changed your mind, or spotted a typo in your address? Here's what you can change, and when.

title: Changing or Cancelling an Order
text: Changing or Cancelling an Order — Before your order is dispatched: Until your order has left our warehouse, you can cancel it or change the delivery address free of charge. There are two ways to do this: Sign in to your account, go to My orders , select the order and choose Cancel order or Change address . Contact our Customer Care team by live chat, email (support@thistleandpine.co.uk) or phone (0113 496 0321) with your order number. Please get in touch as quickly as possible. Orders placed before 1pm on a working day are dispatched the same day, so the window to make changes can be short. If you cancel before dispatch, we refund the full amount, including any delivery charge, to your original payment method.

title: Changing or Cancelling an Order
text: Changing or Cancelling an Order — After your order is dispatched: Once your order has been dispatched it can no longer be cancelled, and we can't change the delivery address. You'll know your order has been dispatched because we'll have emailed you a tracking link. You still have options: Refuse the delivery. If you no longer want the parcel, you can refuse it when the courier arrives. It will be returned to us and we'll refund you once it arrives back at our warehouse. Return it. Accept the parcel and return it within 30 days of delivery using our free Returns Portal at thistleandpine.co.uk/returns.

title: Changing or Cancelling an Order
text: Changing or Cancelling an Order — Adding or swapping items: We can't add items to an order that has already been placed, or swap one item for another. If you've forgotten something, simply place a second order. If you'd like a different item instead, cancel the original (if it hasn't been dispatched) or return it, and place a new order. Discount codes also can't be applied to an order after it has been placed, so please make sure your code is entered at checkout.

title: Changing or Cancelling an Order
text: Changing or Cancelling an Order — Your 14-day cancellation right: Under the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013, you have the right to cancel an online purchase within 14 days without giving a reason. This period starts the day after you receive your goods. If you return your whole order within 14 days, we'll also refund the original delivery charge. Our own 30-day returns policy goes further than the law requires, so most customers simply use the Returns Portal.

title: Changing or Cancelling an Order

title: Changing or Cancelling an Order

location: § How to Care for Your Wooden Chopping Board
text: Wooden Board Care — How to Care for Your Wooden Chopping Board: Last updated: 11 February 2026 A good wooden chopping board will last for years if it's looked after properly. Wood is a natural material that absorbs and releases moisture, so a little regular care keeps it smooth, hygienic and free from cracks. This guide applies to all our wooden chopping, serving and bread boards.

title: Wooden Board Care
text: Wooden Board Care — The golden rules: Hand wash only. Never put a wooden board in the dishwasher. Never soak it. Don't leave your board in a sink of water or submerge it. Oil it monthly with food-safe mineral oil.

title: Wooden Board Care
text: Wooden Board Care — Everyday cleaning: Scrape off any food with the back of a knife or a scraper. Wash both sides with warm water, a little washing-up liquid and a sponge or brush. Rinse quickly under the tap. Dry straight away with a clean tea towel. Leave the board standing upright on its edge to air-dry fully, so both sides dry evenly. Washing both sides, even if you only chopped on one, helps stop the board from warping.

title: Wooden Board Care
text: Wooden Board Care — After raw meat or fish: Wash thoroughly with hot soapy water straight after use. Many cooks prefer to keep one board just for raw meat and another for bread, fruit and vegetables.

title: Wooden Board Care
text: Wooden Board Care — Oiling your board: Oiling stops the wood from drying out and helps it resist moisture and stains. We recommend oiling your board once a month, or whenever it starts to look pale and dry. Make sure the board is clean and completely dry. Pour a small amount of food-safe mineral oil onto the surface. Rub it into the wood with a soft cloth, following the direction of the grain. Don't forget the edges and the underside. Leave it to soak in for a few hours, or overnight. Wipe away any excess oil with a clean cloth. Avoid using cooking oils such as olive or sunflower oil, as they can turn rancid over time and leave an unpleasant smell.

title: Wooden Board Care
text: Wooden Board Care — Removing stains and smells: Sprinkle coarse salt over the board and scrub it with half a lemon. Rinse, dry thoroughly, and re-oil once dry.

title: Wooden Board Care
text: Wooden Board Care — What to avoid: Dishwashers – the heat and water will cause the wood to warp and split. Soaking or leaving the board wet on the draining board. Drying it next to a radiator, oven or in direct sunlight. Using bleach or harsh chemical cleaners.

title: Wooden Board Care
text: Wooden Board Care — Warranty: Our wooden boards are covered by our standard 12-month warranty against manufacturing defects. Splitting or warping caused by dishwasher use or soaking isn't a manufacturing defect and isn't covered, so following this guide really does pay off.
